subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core sender-controlled continuation-marker contract, or keep timer-based inbound debounce and queue collection as the supported batching behavior?
rationale: This is a new user-facing input and configuration mode that changes when agent turns start; repository policy requires maintainer judgment before adding config/default surfaces or a new core/plugin API seam.

options.title: Keep existing batching
options.body: Document and retain timer-based inbound debounce plus collect-mode queueing, avoiding a new marker and configuration contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Define one typed pre-agent aggregation mode with explicit timeout, session ordering, marker removal, command/media handling, and upgrade-safe configuration.

options.title: Add a generic extension seam first
options.body: Expose only the minimum pre-agent admission/buffering hook needed for an external plugin to implement the behavior without channel-specific core policy.

recommendation.title: Keep existing batching
recommendation.body: Document and retain timer-based inbound debounce plus collect-mode queueing, avoiding a new marker and configuration contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature touches the shared inbound-routing ownership boundary and prior maintainer-side review already retained this issue for product follow-up.
